newsitem.title: MEXICO: Maseca awaits new subsidy system in June.
newsitem.headline: Maseca awaits new subsidy system in June.

text.p: The Mexican government is expected to implement a new corn-flour subsidy system in June, Grupo Industrial Maseca SA de CV said on Wednesday.
The government will implement the so-called "electronic card" system in nine state and then take the system nationwide a few months later, Maseca said in a news release.

"In each Mexican state where the system will begin operations, the individual (subsidy) ceilings for producers of corn flour will be eliminated, as will the ceilings for the corn-flour industry and the traditional corn-millers, leaving only the global ceilings for the tortilla industry," Maseca said.
The subsidies are part of a Mexican government program to keep down the cost of tortillas, a pancake made from fresh corn or corn flour that is a staple of the Mexican diet.

But for months food analysts and industry sources have been saying the system needs to be overhauled, both because the system fails to target the poor, subsidizing tortillas for the rich as well, and because of widescale cheating in which subsidized corn flour is being sold at market prices.

Under the electronic card system, tortilla-makers will be given cards that register the amount of fresh corn or corn flour they buy in the open market, and the government will then subsidize them according to what is registered on their cards.

The electronic card system has been favored by Maseca, the overwhelming market leader in Mexican corn flour, because it gives tortilla-makers more flexibility in deciding from whom they wish to buy corn flour.
It also is expected to cut down on the selling of subsidized corn flour on the black market.
Maseca also said that the electronic card system is likely to speed up the ongoing trend of switching from fresh corn to the more efficient corn-flour method for making tortillas.
Share prices for Maseca and its holding company Gruma SA de CV rose on Wednesday when Maseca first said there would be an important announcement on the subsidy program.
But the stock started to fall on Wednesday afternoon when the company said the announcement would be postponed.

The shares recovered before the close when Javier Velez, the CFO for Gruma and Maseca, publicly said the announcement was back on track for Wednesday, coming out with Maseca's first-quarter earnings report.
In March, the Maseca shares took a pounding when the Mexican government said it would not raise the ceiling on subisized corn flour assigned to the industry at a time of increased seasonal demand.
Maseca stock was downgraded by several brokerages until the price sank so low that it was upgraded again by some because it was so cheap.
Analysts then said the best solution for Maseca was either a lifting of the ceiling or drastic changes in the subsidy system such as the electronic card system.
